_comment: What to read out of OVH's AI Endpoints catalog.
It names PRICING UNITS, not models. Which models the catalog offers is OVH's
business and changes week to week; following that is the whole point of this job.
A model OVH adds is published on the next run, one it withdraws keeps its last
observed prices and gains an 'absent_since' stamp, and both show up as + / ~ lines
in the run summary and the commit.
There is no hand-written model list, and there must not be one. The catalog states
the callable model id itself, so nothing needs translating by hand.
The key each model is published under is the catalog entry's 'name' -- NOT its
'id'. The two are different things and it matters: the entry whose id is
'qwen-3-6-27b' is called as 'Qwen3.6-27B', and 'llama-3-3-70b-instruct' is called
as 'Meta-Llama-3_3-70B-Instruct'. 'id' is a CMS slug for the catalog's own URLs.
Fifteen of the nineteen names published on 2026-08-04 were confirmed against OVH's
public OpenAI-compatible model list
(https://oai.endpoints.kepler.ai.cloud.ovh.net/v1/models, no key required); the
four nvr-tts entries are absent from that list because text-to-speech is served
from its own per-model endpoint rather than the OpenAI-compatible one. That
comparison is now run every week by check_coverage.py rather than by hand.
A model the catalog prices at 0 in every unit it states is published with
"free": true and no price field, instead of a price of 0. Nothing is remembered
about which models those are: it is read off the catalog on every run, so a model
that stops being free simply starts showing a price.
A unit missing from the 'units' table below is NOT guessed at. The unit is part of
the field name in pricing.json -- publishing a per-image price under a per-token
key would be worse than publishing nothing -- so that one row is skipped, the run
reports it, and every other price still publishes. 'per_image' and
'million_input_chars' are mapped here even though every model currently using them
is free, so that the day OVH starts charging for one, the price lands in a field
that already says what it means.
This block publishes EUR, which is what the catalog states. No conversion is
performed anywhere in this repository.
